To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) intraneural angiosarcomas are rare tumours; 2) angiosarcomas can also occur in benign nerve sheaths and in malignant peripheral nerve tumours; 3) immunohistochemistry is helpful in confirming both neural and endothelial differentiation; and 4) the expression of vascular endothelial growth factors may play a role in the development of angiosarcomas.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
angiosarcoma is an uncommon form of heterologious differentiation in MPNST, and may also arise in a long-standing peripheral nerve schwannoma.
, in the setting of MPNST, angiosarcoma represents the most common form of heterogenous differentiation, but is also a rare finding in benign nerve sheaths and peripheral nerves.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intraneural angioscarcomas are rare and arise in a variety of settings, but are more commonly seen in association with MPNST.
angiosarcomas arising in benign and/or malignant peripheral nerve sheaths represent a rare form of tumour heterogeneity.
angiosarcoma may arise in benign and malignant nerve sheath tumour, and in peripheral nerves, and that it is not restricted to patients with neurofibroma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunohistochemical profile is a valuable tool to confirm the neural and endothelial lineages of differentiation in these rare lesions.

angiosarcoma is a very rare, but possible, histological subtype of MPNST, and that the presence of a vascular component should not be used as an exclusion criterion when considering a peripheral nerve tumour to be a MPNST.
